Thanks for the question. Seeing records twice and missing others while iterating is the characteristic signature of offset pagination against a collection that is changing underneath you. Cursor pagination avoids this, because the cursor marks a position in the result rather than counting from the start.

Pass the next_cursor value from each response as the cursor parameter of the following request, and stop when it comes back null. Keep page size at or below two hundred, as larger requests are rejected rather than truncated.

One thing to be aware of on long iterations is that cursors expire after an hour, so it is worth recording a checkpoint you can restart from. For very large extracts, the export endpoint is a better fit, as it runs asynchronously and returns a download link.
